title: On-demand micro-rollup layer for long-range usage aggregates
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description: Dashboard queries that request long-range aggregates (30d/90d/365d) currently trigger large fanout scans and expensive compute in the query layer. This increases tail latency and unit cost for common console dashboards (tenant usage, cost breakdowns, model-by-route trends). The proposal is to add an on-demand micro-rollup layer: small materialized aggregates at multiple granularities (hour/day/week) that are created incrementally by a materializer service driven by the ingestion stream and kept TTL'd. The query API will route to rollups using a lightweight cost-based planner, falling back to raw scans when rollups are unavailable or stale beyond an allowed window.
acceptance_criteria: 95th-percentile query latency for 30-day aggregated dashboard endpoints <= 250ms in canary tenants
Mean per-query compute cost for long-range aggregates reduced by >= 70% vs current production baseline
Rollup staleness never exceeds configured threshold (default 2 minutes) under normal ingestion rates
Graceful fallback path: when rollup is stale or missing, query planner selects partial rollup + incremental scan to bound latency/cost
Dark launch across 10% of tenants with hit-rate and correctness monitoring before full rollout
Observability: new dashboards for rollup hit-rate, materializer lag, storage usage, and cost savings
updates: 2026-02-12: Spike analysis completed — identified that 72% of CPU spent on 30d/90d aggregates originates from repeated scans across the same time buckets; median cardinality per tenant is low (<500 routes) but tail tenants cause most cost.

2026-02-18: Design doc reviewed with Analytics and Infra (see Confluence link). Decided on multi-granularity rollups (1h, 24h, 7d) and tenant-size tiering (small tenants use single shared table partitions; large tenants get dedicated time-partitioned shards).
2026-02-25: Prototype materializer that consumes usage-events topic and emits incremental deltas; initial correctness tests pass for counts and sums (PR #4123).

2026-03-03: Benchmarks on staging: cold raw 30d scan median latency 1.6s -> rollup-backed median 120ms; p95 raw 3.8s -> rollup p95 210ms. Cost model simulation shows ~73% token/compute reduction for sample tenant mix.

2026-03-08: Design review feedback: add HLL-based approximate distinct for high-cardinality groups to reduce rollup size; agreed to store accuracy metadata per rollup to allow queries to choose exact vs approximate paths.

2026-03-11: Blocker found — schema migration for time-partitioned index (Postgres -> ClickHouse) requires infra migration task (dep ENG-771234). Planning canary rollout with 5% tenants while infra migration is scheduled.
2026-03-12: Implemented cost-based planner thresholds and dark-launch flags. Instrumentation added to Console to surface hit-rate, staleness, and per-query chosen path in traces.
Next steps: finish infra migration, run 2-week canary, and prepare runbook for failures and rollbacks.
notes_on_implementation: Materializer: a small stateful service consuming the usage-events Kafka topic; performs incremental aggregation by tenant+metric+time-bucket and writes to a time-partitioned rollup store (ClickHouse for high-volume tenants, small Postgres tables for low-volume tenants).
Granularities: 1h for near-term, 24h for month-level, 7d for quarter-level. Rollups are generated lazily (on-demand) for older ranges and proactively for the most-accessed tenants/buckets.

Planner: cost-based decision uses rollup hit probability, expected IO, and allowed staleness; planner returns one of: rollup-only, rollup+delta-scan, raw-scan. Thresholds are configurable per tenant class.
Staleness model: materializer writes a watermark per rollup. Queries will accept rollups <= 2 minutes old by default; configurable per dashboard route.
Storage/TTL: rollups have TTLs based on granularity (1h rollups TTL 14d, 24h TTL 400d) to cap storage. Cold rollups can be regenerated on demand but with higher cost.
Approximate metrics: use HyperLogLog for distinct counts when cardinality > configured threshold; accuracy metadata attached to rollup to allow opt-in exact computations.
Observability: add rollup_hit boolean and chosen_path tag to traces, push materializer lag histogram, and per-tenant storage delta metric to Console telemetry.
Rollout plan: dark launch -> canary (5%) -> expanded canary (25%) -> gradual rollout with capacity guardrails and automatic rollback on regression of p95 latency or incorrect aggregates.
test_benchmarks: Baseline: sample-50 tenants long-range aggregate median latency 1.6s, p95 3.8s, average CPU cost 1.0 compute-unit/query
Rollup-backed (staging prototype): median 120ms, p95 210ms, average CPU cost 0.27 compute-unit/query (~73% reduction)
Worst-case fallback (partial rollup + delta scan): median 320ms, p95 650ms
Storage delta: expected additional storage ~12GB/day for combined rollups across all tenants in sample cluster (configurable by TTL)
